title: Unshared task: (Dis)agreement in online debates
authors: Maria Skeppstedt; Magnus Sahlgren; Carita Paradis; Andreas Kerren
venue: Proceedings of the Third Workshop on Argument Mining
task_description: Detect topic-independent sentence-level agreement versus disagreement in web-forum debates; includes a shared-task-style evaluation and classifier baselines.
inputs: Forum-debate sentences; 27 discussion threads; an additional 2,000-sentence evaluation set.
outputs_or_labels: Agreement, disagreement, or neither; 175 manually annotated expressions (43 agreement, 132 disagreement); reported precision/recall/F-scores.
artifact_access_status: PDF and ACL landing page accessible
evidence_basis: ACL page/PDF and search evidence: corpus of 27 threads; 175 expressions; 2,000 sentences; 10-fold results and classifier scores.
limitations: Detects overt discourse relations, not proposition-level shared premises; small expression inventory and online-forum domain.
why_relevant: Direct precedent for recognizing whether an opposing turn accepts or rejects a prior argument, useful as a relation layer before extracting common commitments.

title: I Couldn't Agree More: The Role of Conversational Structure in Agreement and Disagreement Detection in Online Discussions
venue: Proceedings of the 16th Annual Meeting of SIGDIAL
benchmark_or_resource_name: Agreement by Create Debaters (ABCD) plus IAC/AWTP comparison
task_description: Three-way classification of a quote-response pair as agreement, disagreement, or none, exploiting thread structure and naturally derived side labels.
inputs: Quote-response pairs from online debate forums; ABCD from CreateDebate plus IAC and AWTP comparison corpora.
outputs_or_labels: Agreement, disagreement, none; ABCD reported as 9,981 threads and 185,479 posts in the retained PDF evidence; IAC scalar agreement converted to classes.
artifact_access_status: ACL PDF accessible; dataset release URL cited in paper
license_status: License not verified from retained evidence
evidence_basis: ACL PDF/search evidence: three-way task; ABCD 25 times larger than prior corpus; IAC uses -5 to +5 agreement scores; paper reports dataset release.
limitations: Labels relation to adjacent post, not which propositions or premises are jointly accepted; derived side labels may encode stance rather than explicit agreement.
why_relevant: Best established benchmark family for agreement/common-ground precursor detection in adversarial online argument threads.

title: ClaimDiff: Comparing and Contrasting Claims on Contentious Issues
authors: Miyoung Ko; Ingyu Seong; Hwaran Lee; Joonsuk Park; Minsuk Chang; Minjoon Seo
task_description: Compare claims from different documents on the same contentious issue and classify whether one claim strengthens or weakens the other; extract human rationales.
inputs: Pairs of claims from articles sharing a topic, plus article/topic metadata.
outputs_or_labels: Strengthen or weaken relation, unrelated/negative cases in full test distribution, and extractive rationale spans; 2,941 claim pairs reported by ACL/GitHub.
pipeline_gap_filled: cross-tradition argument form and strength evaluation
artifact_access_status: ACL page and GitHub repository accessible
license_status: Repository license not verified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: ACL landing page/PDF search evidence and official GitHub README: 2,941 claim pairs; ClaimDiff-S/W; rationale field; train/test/test-full files.
limitations: The target is comparative influence, not explicit mutual acceptance; source articles are trusted news and not necessarily dialogically responding.
why_relevant: A close benchmark for identifying overlap and directional compatibility between claims before synthesizing shared ground; rationales expose inspectable evidence.

title: ArgCMV: An Argument Summarization Benchmark for the LLM-era
authors: Omkar Gurjar; Agam Goyal; Eshwar Chandrasekharan
benchmark_or_resource_name: ArgCMV shared key-point extraction and matching
task_description: Extract stance-specific key points from long multi-turn ChangeMyView debates, map each argument to its realized key points, and evaluate pairwise shared-key-point detection/generation.
inputs: 12,262 arguments from 3,131 Reddit r/ChangeMyView topics; pro/con argument pools; topic and stance; argument-to-key-point mappings.
outputs_or_labels: Key points, mappings, stance +1/-1, shared-key-point yes/no plus generated shared key point in pairwise formulation; manual validation of generated mappings.
pipeline_gap_filled: provenance/dependency-preserving selection/compression and synthesis from shared ground
artifact_access_status: ACL paper and GitHub repository accessible
license_status: Repository states anonymized IDs and policy constraints; exact license not verified
evidence_basis: ACL PDF/search evidence: 12K arguments, 3K topics, opposing pools, cross-user convergence, shared-KP pairwise baseline; official GitHub README confirms train/dev/test and kp fields.
limitations: Key points are model-assisted and stance-specific; shared KP may mean same-side convergence and is not a formal premise accepted by both opposing sides; Reddit IDs require rehydration.
why_relevant: Strongest direct benchmark found for synthesis from shared argumentative ground across opposing lines: it exposes argument-level mappings and shared abstractions rather than only final summaries.

title: The Argument Reasoning Comprehension Task: Identification and Reconstruction of Implicit Warrants
authors: Ivan Habernal; Henning Wachsmuth; Iryna Gurevych; Benno Stein
task_description: Given a premise, claim, topic, and two plausible lexically close warrants that imply opposite claims, select the warrant that reconstructs the intended reasoning.
inputs: Authentic English arguments from online debate sources; premise, claim, topic, and two candidate warrants.
outputs_or_labels: Binary correct-warrant choice; 1,970 instances; accuracy; best shared-task result 0.712 reported in the paper.
pipeline_gap_filled: cross-tradition argument form and implicit premise recovery
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF and GitHub repository accessible
license_status: Repository license not verified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: ACL PDF/search evidence explicitly states 1,970 instances, opposing candidate warrants, authentic English arguments, and binary accuracy task; official GitHub artifact found.
limitations: Only one argument at a time; warrant is an implicit bridge, not a proposition shared by two opposing arguments; no cross-line agreement label.
why_relevant: Operationalizes the hidden-assumption component needed to test whether two opposing arguments share a premise or warrant after explicit premises are normalized.

title: Finding Common Ground: Annotating and Predicting Common Ground in Spoken Conversations
authors: Magdalena Markowska; Mohammad Taghizadeh; Adil Soubki; Seyed Mirroshandel; Owen Rambow
task_description: Annotate propositions, participant beliefs, and common-ground updates in natural spoken conversations; evaluate proposition extraction and common-ground tracking.
inputs: Natural spoken dialogue from CALLHOME; turns, propositions/events, participant-perspective beliefs, and discourse context.
outputs_or_labels: Belief statuses and common-ground update types, including just-added/already-in-common-ground/rejected/not-applicable style labels; proposition extraction and tracking scores.
pipeline_gap_filled: inspectable philosophical output and shared-commitment tracking
artifact_access_status: ACL landing page and linked GitHub organization accessible
license_status: Dataset/license details not verified from retained evidence
evidence_basis: ACL abstract/search evidence says it introduces an annotation and corpus for common ground and experiments extracting propositions and tracking their status from each speaker's perspective.
limitations: Not argumentative or adversarial; common ground is conversational belief state rather than intersection of premises in opposing argument structures.
why_relevant: Useful control and annotation design for representing shared commitments and updates once argument-specific relation detection has identified candidate propositions.

title: Views Are My Own, but Also Yours: Benchmarking Theory of Mind Using Common Ground
authors: Adil Soubki; John Murzaku; Arash Yousefi Jordehi; Peter Zeng; Magdalena Markowska; Seyed Mirroshandel; Owen Rambow
task_description: Question-answering benchmark over naturally occurring spoken dialogues that tests whether a system tracks what each participant believes is in common ground.
inputs: CALLHOME-derived dyadic spoken dialogs; propositions/events and belief/common-ground annotations; generated questions.
outputs_or_labels: Answers about participant beliefs and common-ground status; belief categories and common-ground update states are represented in the underlying corpus.
pipeline_gap_filled: inspectable philosophical output and shared-commitment tracking
artifact_access_status: ACL page and official GitHub repository accessible
license_status: Repository license not verified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: ACL/PDF search evidence: natural-dialogue benchmark, explicit common-ground representation, and official common-tom repository; search evidence reports CALLHOME basis and belief/CG states.
limitations: Not opposition-focused and QA formulation can hide the intermediate proposition alignment; limited to English spoken dialogue.
why_relevant: Provides a reusable evaluation pattern for testing whether a model distinguishes a speaker's view from mutually shared commitments, a core failure mode in common-ground detection.

title: I do not disagree: Leveraging Monolingual Alignment to Detect Disagreement in Dialogue
task_description: Classify agreement/disagreement for quote-response pairs using semantic alignment features between the quoted and responding sentences.
inputs: IAC quote-response pairs from political online debate; human agreement scores from -5 to +5; roughly 6,000 valid pairs reported in search evidence.
outputs_or_labels: Agreement/disagreement/none derived from scalar scores; retrieval/classification accuracy, including disagreement retrieval improvement from 69% to 77%.
license_status: Dataset license not verified in retained evidence
evidence_basis: ACL PDF/search evidence identifies IAC, human-annotated agreement scale, quote-response inputs, and reported improvement for disagreement-pair retrieval.
limitations: Focuses on pair-level relation and alignment, without proposition decomposition or explicit shared-premise labels; relies on an existing corpus.
why_relevant: A useful relation-detection baseline and evidence that lexical/semantic alignment can recover acceptance/rejection signals in opposing online arguments.
